newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to refrain from open money market operations on Thursday with the overnight bank lending rate trading substantially below its 5.25-percent target, economists said.
"Funds are well below target," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and an economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.
"They also have that nine-day fixed (system repurchase agreement) on the books, so that's contributing to that mass of funds that is available," he added.
The overnight bank lending, or federal funds rate, was trading at 5.0 percent just after 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. Funds closed at 5.5 percent on Wednesday after averaging 4.96 percent.
